deck.title: Cost Management Tools
deck.analogy: Your AWS bill is a household budget: Cost Explorer is the bank app, Budgets the spending alarm, CUR the shoebox of receipts, Anomaly Detection the suspicious spouse, Compute Optimizer the personal trainer.

cards.front: How should you think of the AWS cost tools, and how does the exam test them?

back.answer: Think of a household budget; the exam asks you to pick the right tool from a verb.
back.explanation: You never need to master the tools, only match the verb (see, alert, raw detail, unusual, rightsize) to the tool.
back.mnemonic: Bank app (Explorer), spending alarm (Budgets), shoebox of receipts (CUR), suspicious spouse (Anomaly), personal trainer (Compute Optimizer).

cards.front: What does AWS Cost Explorer do?

back.answer: Visualizes and filters historical spend, forecasts ~12 months ahead, and gives RI/Savings Plan purchase recommendations.
back.explanation: Signal words: analyze, visualize, which service drives the bill.
back.mnemonic: The bank app where you browse where the money went.

cards.front: What does AWS Budgets do?

back.answer: Sets cost or usage thresholds and alerts (or triggers actions) when actual or forecast spend crosses them.
back.explanation: Signal words: notify, alert at 80%, exceeds.
back.mnemonic: The spending alarm on your phone.

cards.front: What is the AWS Cost & Usage Report (CUR) and how is it queried?

back.answer: The most detailed line-item billing data, delivered to S3 and queried with Athena (or QuickSight).
back.explanation: Signal words: granular, most detailed, line items, SQL.
back.mnemonic: The shoebox of every raw receipt.

cards.front: What does AWS Cost Anomaly Detection do?

back.answer: Uses machine learning to watch spend and alert on unusual spikes, with no thresholds needed.
back.mnemonic: The suspicious spouse noticing triple the usual takeout.

cards.front: What does AWS Compute Optimizer do, and for which resources?

back.answer: ML rightsizing recommendations for EC2, EBS volumes, Lambda and Auto Scaling groups.
back.explanation: Signal words: overprovisioned, rightsize, recommend instance size.
back.mnemonic: The personal trainer saying your membership is too big.

cards.front: What are AWS Cost Allocation Tags used for, and what must you do first?

back.answer: Tag resources (team/project) and slice costs by tag; tags must be activated in the Billing console.
back.explanation: Signal words: cost per team/department/project, chargeback.

cards.front: Where do you get Savings Plan / Reserved Instance purchase recommendations in AWS cost tooling?

back.answer: Cost Explorer recommends purchases based on your historical usage.
back.explanation: Savings Plans and RIs are the commitment discounts themselves; Explorer only recommends them.

cards.front: What is AWS Billing Conductor for?

back.answer: Building customized (pro forma) billing views and rates to show costs to internal groups or customers.

cards.front: A scenario wants a notification when spending hits X% of budget. Why is Cost Explorer the decoy?

back.answer: Budgets alerts, Explorer analyzes: Explorer has forecasts but doesn't notify, and Budgets doesn't give historical breakdowns.
back.explanation: Threshold plus notify always means AWS Budgets.

cards.front: Do cost allocation tags apply retroactively to billing data?

back.answer: No — a tag only appears in billing data after you activate it, and only for usage from then on.
back.explanation: Activation in the Billing console is required and is not retroactive or automatic.

cards.front: What is the decision line for picking an AWS cost tool?

back.answer: SEE: Explorer. ALERT: Budgets. RAW detail: CUR + Athena. UNUSUAL: Anomaly Detection. RIGHTSIZE: Compute Optimizer. Per-team chargeback: Cost Allocation Tags.

cards.front: Receive a notification when forecasted spend reaches 80% of the monthly budget. Which AWS tool?

back.explanation: Threshold plus notify is Budgets every time.

choices.why: Analyzes and forecasts but doesn't alert.

cards.front: Finance must attribute AWS costs to individual teams and projects. Which approach?

back.explanation: Tag, activate in billing, slice the bill.

choices.why: Activated tags let you split costs by team.

cards.front: Analysts need the most granular billing data, queryable with standard SQL. Which solution?

back.explanation: Detailed line items land in S3; Athena provides SQL.

choices.why: Line items in S3 queried via SQL.

cards.front: Identify overprovisioned EC2 instances and get sizing recommendations. Which tool?
Get alerted about unexpected spending spikes without setting thresholds. Which tool?

back.explanation: ML learns normal spend and flags unusual.

cards.front: Understand which service caused last month's bill increase and forecast next quarter. Which tool?
Decide how much Savings Plan commitment to purchase. Which tool helps?
